newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end lower, nearbys limit-down.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end lower, nearbys limit-down.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended lower in all months, with nearby two months down by the daily 500 yen limit, as local investors were discouraged by the Chicago market's price losses overnight, traders said.
The benchmark September 1997 contract was down 250 yen at 16,150. Daily volume was 111,573 lots.
Selling by individual investors pushed down the market from the opening, the traders said. Investors liquidated long positions ahead of the long weekend, they said.
The weaker CBOT overnight corn trading accentuated the bearish sentiment in Tokyo, they said.
The Tokyo corn futures market will be closed on Monday due to a national holiday. Trading will resume on Tuesday.

The December contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $3.12-1/2 per bushel at 0810 GMT, against its $3.13-1/2 close on Thursday. November CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system were at $7.89-3/4 at 0810 GMT, against Thursday's closing price of $7.89-1/4.
